related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take to reduce COVID symptoms?
related_questions.snippet: Take an over-the-counter medicine such as acetaminophen or ibuprofen. These can be used as a fever reducer or to treat headache, sore throat or body aches. While ibuprofen will reduce your fever, there is some concern that it may not be safe to take with the novel coronavirus.

related_questions.question: How to get COVID out of your system?

text_blocks.snippet: To get COVID-19 out of your system, focus on rest, hydration, and managing symptoms. While there's no specific cure to remove the virus, your body's immune system will naturally work to fight it off. Symptom management can include over-the-counter medications for fever and pain, and ensuring adequate fluid intake.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and managing symptoms

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Allow your body to focus on healing by getting plenty of sleep and avoiding strenuous activities.

list.title: Isolation:
list.snippet: To prevent spreading the virus, isolate yourself from others, especially those at higher risk of severe illness.

list.title: Fever and Pain:
list.snippet: Use over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) to manage fever and aches.

list.title: Cough and Congestion:
list.snippet: Consider using a cool mist humidifier or taking a warm, steamy shower to help loosen congestion and ease breathing, says UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, as dehydration can worsen symptoms.

list.title: When to Seek Medical Advice:
list.snippet: If you experience severe symptoms like persistent fever, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or confusion, seek immediate medical attention.

list.title: Treatment Options:
list.snippet: A doctor can assess your condition and may recommend specific treatments or medications depending on the severity of your illness.

list.title: Lukewarm Baths:
list.snippet: A lukewarm bath can help regulate body temperature and boost circulation, especially if you have a fever.

list.title: Steam Inhalation:
list.snippet: Inhaling steam from a bowl of hot water or a warm shower can help loosen congestion according to UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Avoid Overbundling:
list.snippet: If you have a fever, avoid overdressing or bundling up, as this can trap heat.

list.title: Recovery Time:
list.snippet: Mild to moderate COVID-19 cases typically resolve within one to two weeks, says UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Listen to Your Body:
list.snippet: Pay attention to your body's signals and allow for a gradual return to normal activities as you recover.

related_questions.question: How to speed up recovery from COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: To speed up recovery from COVID-19, focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management. Get plenty of sleep, stay hydrated by drinking lots of fluids, and consider over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever or body aches. Additionally, it's crucial to isolate to prevent spreading the virus and monitor your health for any worsening symptoms.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on rest, hydration, and symptom management

text_blocks.snippet: Key strategies for faster COVID-19 recovery:

list.title: Rest and Sleep:
list.snippet: Prioritize rest and aim for more sleep than usual, exceeding the recommended 7-9 hours for adults, according to UnityPoint Health.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids, such as water, broth, or electrolyte drinks, to stay hydrated.

list.title: Over-the-counter Medications:
list.snippet: Use over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) to manage fever and body aches.

list.title: Isolate and Monitor:
list.snippet: Stay home to prevent the spread of COVID-19 and closely monitor your symptoms for any signs of worsening, such as difficulty breathing or persistent high fever.

list.title: Seek Medical Advice:
list.snippet: If you experience severe symptoms or have underlying health conditions, consult a doctor for guidance on managing your recovery.

list.title: Healthy Diet:
list.snippet: While not a quick fix, eating a balanced diet with plenty of fruits and vegetables can support your body's immune system during recovery.

list.title: Manage Stress:
list.snippet: Find healthy ways to manage stress and anxiety, as stress can affect your immune system.

text_blocks.snippet: Remember that recovery time varies, but these measures can help you feel better sooner and potentially shorten the duration of your illness.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to recover from COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Early research suggested that it could take two weeks for your body to get over a mild illness or up to six weeks for severe or critical cases. Recovery varies for different people, depending on things like your age and overall health. Fatigue, headache, and troubled breathing are the symptoms most likely to linger.
